survival-story.name: Survival Story
survival-story.summary: Narrative arc of overcoming adversity through determination: catastrophe, backstory, plan, danger, effort, struggle, pivot, breakthrough, legacy, takeaway. For brand stories, founder histories, and leadership talks where the lesson lives in the comeback.

beats.name: Catastrophe
beats.description: Open in the middle of the disaster. Specific moment, specific stakes, specific damage. Drop the audience into the worst point of the story before walking them back.

beats.name: Backstory
beats.description: Detail the events that led up to the catastrophe. Just enough for the audience to understand how the disaster could have happened. Avoid moralizing — the story does the work.

beats.name: Blueprint
beats.description: Illustrate the recovery plan. Specific moves, specific bets, specific people. The audience should see the strategy as more than 'try hard.'

beats.name: Danger
beats.description: Highlight the emerging threats to the recovery plan. New risks, returning ones. Tension here makes the eventual triumph credible.

beats.name: Endeavor
beats.description: Show the determined effort underway. The hours, the trade-offs, the discipline. The audience must feel the work, not just hear about it.

beats.name: Struggles
beats.description: Showcase challenging moments along the way: the setbacks, the false starts, the hard calls. Honest setbacks make eventual success feel earned.

beats.name: Pivot
beats.description: Highlight the strategic shift that changed the trajectory. What got reconsidered, what got dropped, what got doubled down on. The pivot is the moment the protagonist became something new.

beats.name: Breakthrough
beats.description: Emphasize the moment adversity finally broke. Concrete result, concrete date. Let the slide land — the audience came for this turn.

beats.name: Legacy
beats.description: Discuss the enduring impact. What survival made possible afterward, who benefited, what was built on top. Survival stories are most powerful when they create more than they restore.

beats.name: Takeaway
beats.description: Share the lesson the audience can carry away. One transferable insight, framed for their own challenges — not a general moral.

internal-team.name: Internal Team
internal-team.summary: Company employees across functions receiving operational updates, project status, or training content.
internal-team.description: Employees across functions receiving operational updates, project status, or training. Make next steps, owners, and progress visible, and state action items explicitly. Moderate chart density; 10-20 slides.

persuade.name: Persuade
persuade.summary: Change belief or win support for a specific argument, idea, or recommendation.
persuade.description: Use when the audience may be skeptical or undecided. Build a crisp thesis, support it with evidence, address objections, and end with a clear action.
persuade.outcome: The audience accepts the argument or supports the recommendation.

persuasive.name: Persuasive
persuasive.summary: Argument-led voice for sales, fundraising, and recommendation-driven decks.
persuasive.description: Frame every section as an argument that builds toward an ask. Surface objections, answer them, and pair claims with the strongest available proof. Read more like a memo than a report.
voiceCues: Lead each section with the claim it's making.
Surface the strongest counter-argument and address it.
Pair every claim with proof — customer, benchmark, or analyst.
End on a clear ask with named owner and date.
avoid: Symmetrical 'on one hand / on the other' framing without a verdict.
Information for its own sake — every chart should advance the argument.
Passive endings without a clear ask.
samplePhrases: Adopting our runtime cuts inference latency 8× while preserving accuracy.
The most common objection — 'we'll be locked in' — is addressed by our open OPF spec.
We're asking for a $30M Series B to ship into the enterprise tier.

bold.name: Bold
bold.description: A vibrant, high-energy theme with bold colors and a dynamic, attention-grabbing style. Great for presentations that need to stand out.

steel-blue.name: Steel Blue
steel-blue.summary: Cool steel blues for credible, data-forward presentations.
steel-blue.description: A steel-blue palette that combines credibility, precision, and calm. Useful for analysis-heavy decks.

burnt-orange.name: Burnt Orange
burnt-orange.summary: Warm orange and red accents for energetic commercial decks.
burnt-orange.description: A warm, high-contrast palette built around burnt orange, red, navy, and gold. It feels active without losing structure.

noto-sans.name: Noto Sans
noto-sans.description: Noto Sans is a sans serif OPF font scheme for complex script presentations, using Noto Sans for both headings and body text.

impact.name: Impact
impact.description: Impact is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Impact for headings with Grandview for body text.

cover.name: Cover
cover.summary: The opening slide: title, subtitle and an optional picture.
cover.description: Open a presentation with its subject and a short introduction. Add a picture when it helps establish the context.

text.name: Text
text.summary: Prose. Several blocks sit side by side when short and stack when long.
text.description: Explain one idea in continuous prose. Use paragraphs or flowing blocks for detail that needs to be read in sequence.

chart.name: Chart
chart.summary: One to six charts, with an optional note.
chart.description: Give a chart enough space to show its evidence. Use the title to state the conclusion and labels to explain the measures.

list.name: List
list.summary: Bulleted or numbered points; one long list flows into columns.
list.description: Present several related points in a clear sequence. Use bullets for independent points or numbered items for an ordered list.
